name: Mara Bell
coverage: An original branching campaign: recurring cast, remembered choices and three alternate endings.

chapters.title: The offer
chapters.text: A harbour clerk leaves Mara a ledger before vanishing. Dockworker Len says the numbers describe people, not just cargo.

chapters.title: People and limits
chapters.text: Len offers introductions to the families named in the ledger. An accountant, Ivo, will help if their names stay private.

choices.label: Promise more than I can know

chapters.title: The shortcut
chapters.text: A publisher offers Mara money for an accusation before the records have been checked. The money would solve her rent problem.

choices.label: Slow down and verify the offer

chapters.title: A decision with a cost
chapters.text: The ledger points to a relief fund that never reached the harbour. A council hearing is coming, and so is another storm.

chapters.title: The shared plan
chapters.text: Residents offer testimony, but some need protection from public attention. Mara must decide what evidence can be shared responsibly.

choices.label: Record consent, access and the missing work

chapters.title: The private bargain
chapters.text: The fund director offers a quiet settlement in exchange for silence. Ivo refuses to be anyone's invented alibi.

choices.label: Negotiate safeguards and publish the terms

chapters.title: The handover
chapters.text: At the hearing, Len asks Mara to distinguish what she knows from what she suspects. The city needs an answer it can act on.

choices.label: Keep the advantage and the secret

chapters.title: A shared future
chapters.text: The relief fund is reopened under public scrutiny. Mara has no triumphant headline; she has named people who can finally collect what was owed.

chapters.title: An unfinished future
chapters.text: The hearing brings a partial remedy. Some records remain sealed, and Mara keeps working with Len rather than pretending every wrong was solved.

chapters.title: A costly victory
chapters.text: The accusation became a spectacle. Mara kept the payment, lost the witnesses' trust, and now owns a story whose missing facts follow her.

name: Tavi Sol
coverage: An original branching campaign: recurring cast, remembered choices and three alternate endings.

chapters.title: The offer
chapters.text: A dust storm isolates Tavi's greenhouse from the settlement. Engineer Rue and cook Nemi disagree over who should receive the remaining crop.

chapters.title: People and limits
chapters.text: Rue brings a repair plan with a hard limit: enough power for one working section, not the whole greenhouse.

choices.label: Promise more than I can know

chapters.title: The shortcut
chapters.text: A sponsor offers a new system if Tavi gives its staff first access to the crop. The offer is real; so are the people excluded by it.

choices.label: Slow down and verify the offer

chapters.title: A decision with a cost
chapters.text: The settlement votes on priorities while the seeds are still viable. Nemi asks for a plan that explains scarcity without disguising favouritism.

chapters.title: The shared plan
chapters.text: The shared plan needs rotations, training and accessible work. One volunteer can no longer lift the equipment they used to handle.

choices.label: Record consent, access and the missing work

chapters.title: The private bargain
chapters.text: The sponsor wants control of the next harvest. Rue asks whether a smaller independent greenhouse would be a better promise.

choices.label: Negotiate safeguards and publish the terms

chapters.title: The handover
chapters.text: The first crop returns. Tavi must name the collaborators and decide how the next generation will learn to maintain it.

choices.label: Keep the advantage and the secret

chapters.title: A shared future
chapters.text: The greenhouse belongs to a working cooperative. It is smaller than the old vision and stronger than a promise no one could maintain.

chapters.title: An unfinished future
chapters.text: Tavi accepts a limited partnership with a public access agreement. Rue stays wary, and the settlement keeps reviewing the terms.

chapters.title: A costly victory
chapters.text: The crop survives behind a private gate. Tavi saved the greenhouse and made the settlement's hunger someone else's unanswered concern.

name: Oren Vale
coverage: An original branching campaign: recurring cast, remembered choices and three alternate endings.

chapters.title: The offer
chapters.text: Oren is asked to serve as regent while the heir recovers. Archivist Sera presents an oath that promises service, not permanent possession of power.

chapters.title: People and limits
chapters.text: Sera proposes open petitions with accessible routes for people who cannot travel to court. The treasurer warns that court spectacle is cheaper.

choices.label: Promise more than I can know

chapters.title: The shortcut
chapters.text: A noble coalition offers Oren a comfortable reign if petitions remain private. Their support would be useful and conditional.

choices.label: Slow down and verify the offer

chapters.title: A decision with a cost
chapters.text: A town bridge fails. Builders, merchants and carers disagree about who should receive the first limited funds.

chapters.title: The shared plan
chapters.text: The public plan will require fewer banquets and an honest report about what the crown cannot yet repair.

choices.label: Record consent, access and the missing work

chapters.title: The private bargain
chapters.text: The coalition offers to fund the bridge in exchange for control of its tolls. The heir asks who will live with the agreement after Oren leaves.

choices.label: Negotiate safeguards and publish the terms

chapters.title: The handover
chapters.text: The heir can return. Oren must hand over a readable account of promises, money, collaborators and unfinished work.

choices.label: Keep the advantage and the secret

chapters.title: A shared future
chapters.text: Oren returns the crown with a public record and a modest repaired bridge. The oath became a practice rather than a flattering story.

chapters.title: An unfinished future
chapters.text: The crown returns with a negotiated toll limit and public review. The town gets a bridge and a continuing argument worth having.

chapters.title: A costly victory
chapters.text: Oren keeps the title but loses the open petitions. Power remains; the people whose needs justified it can no longer reach the room.

name: Jules Reed
coverage: An original branching campaign: recurring cast, remembered choices and three alternate endings.

chapters.title: The offer
chapters.text: Jules wakes on a familiar first day at a job they left ten years ago. Friend Mina remembers none of the future Jules carries.

chapters.title: People and limits
chapters.text: Mina offers a slow introduction to the team. Jules could use old knowledge carefully without promising certainty they do not have.

choices.label: Promise more than I can know

chapters.title: The shortcut
chapters.text: A manager wants Jules to predict a market shift and claim it as expertise. The offer brings status and a fragile invented explanation.

choices.label: Slow down and verify the offer

chapters.title: A decision with a cost
chapters.text: A former mistake approaches in an unfamiliar form. Jules cannot know whether changing one decision will produce the future they expect.

chapters.title: The shared plan
chapters.text: Jules can share the concern as a possibility and ask the people involved what they want. Mina reminds them that care is not control.

choices.label: Record consent, access and the missing work

chapters.title: The private bargain
chapters.text: The manager offers secrecy in exchange for a rapid promotion. Jules would gain influence over people who never agreed to become an experiment.

choices.label: Negotiate safeguards and publish the terms

chapters.title: The handover
chapters.text: The day finally moves beyond the memory. Jules must choose whether to keep living through borrowed certainty or build a life with the people actually here.

choices.label: Keep the advantage and the secret

chapters.title: A shared future
chapters.text: Jules lets the old future go. Mina remains a friend, the team makes its own choices, and a second first day becomes an ordinary next day.

chapters.title: An unfinished future
chapters.text: Jules keeps a private notebook of possibilities. Some relationships survive, some change, and the future refuses to become a guaranteed result.

chapters.title: A costly victory
chapters.text: Jules gets the promotion and loses the honest explanation. The future changes anyway; control was never the certainty it seemed.

name: Robin Vale
coverage: An original night-shift drama: a recurring cafe crew, competing needs and three alternate endings.

chapters.title: The last open door
chapters.text: Robin takes over a tiny late-night cafe. Cook Deni wants predictable hours. Driver Sol wants the only warm room left open after midnight.

choices.label: Ask what the place needs to be
Plan a profitable late service first

chapters.title: The shared table
chapters.text: Deni proposes closing one quiet night each week. Sol says that is the night drivers most need somewhere to wait.

choices.label: Try rotating nights and review together

chapters.title: The queue
chapters.text: A delivery platform brings orders and fees. Sol waits while Deni handles food for strangers who never enter the room.

choices.label: Limit deliveries to what the kitchen can manage
Take the volume and discuss a paid extra shift

chapters.title: The locked drawer
chapters.text: Sol finds an old notebook of customer tabs. Some are debts; some were quietly forgiven. Robin cannot tell which from a number alone.

choices.label: Ask before turning memories into invoices
Separate current accounts from old stories

chapters.title: The extra shift
chapters.text: Deni will work later for better pay, but asks what happens when a tired person makes a mistake.

choices.label: Build a shorter menu and a relief plan
Pay the shift and accept a narrower safety margin

chapters.title: An empty bus stop
chapters.text: A cancelled bus strands six people. Hosting them costs time and heat; turning them away protects a crew already past closing.

choices.label: Offer a limited warm wait and share the work
Help them find transport, then close

chapters.title: The deposit
chapters.text: The landlord offers a longer lease with a larger deposit. Sol suggests a regular drivers table. Deni wants Robin to stop promising every kind of cafe at once.

choices.label: Choose the drivers table and a smaller menu
Choose a shorter lease and a profitable core

chapters.title: The meeting before dawn
chapters.text: The crew agrees the cafe cannot serve everyone all night. The question is whether Robin has made room for a plan they can actually keep.

choices.label: Share the decision and the responsibilities
Keep control and a tighter business plan

chapters.title: The first quiet morning
chapters.text: A viable plan means some customers lose their old routine. Robin has to explain a change instead of disguising it as a miracle.

choices.label: Keep a smaller service with honest limits
Build a cooperative plan with the crew

chapters.title: A light kept on
chapters.text: Deni has a real night off. Sol still has a table on the nights they agreed. Robin leaves a rota anyone can read: the cafe survives because the promise has edges.

chapters.title: A smaller good thing
chapters.text: The cafe closes earlier. Not every old customer stays, but the crew can keep the work going. Robin learns that a smaller useful place is still a place worth keeping.

chapters.title: The busy window
chapters.text: Orders pour through the pickup window. The cafe earns enough to remain open, while Deni and Sol make new arrangements elsewhere. Robin has a business and a different kind of silence.

name: Ellis Reed
coverage: An original family mystery: an inherited house, conflicting memories and three alternate resolutions.

chapters.title: A key and three letters
chapters.text: Ellis inherits a small house. Brother Kit thinks it should be sold. Former neighbour June has a letter saying she once paid for its roof.

choices.label: Hear Kit and June before deciding
Inventory the house and its records first

chapters.title: The guest room
chapters.text: Kit remembers being sent away from this room. June remembers it sheltering her child. The same house has held very different stories.

choices.label: Keep both accounts in the record
Ask for documents before discussing money

chapters.title: The roof receipt
chapters.text: The receipt shows June paid, but a note says the payment was a gift. Neither detail establishes what was promised later.

choices.label: Show the note to June and ask
Keep the financial question separate for now

chapters.title: The second letter
chapters.text: A letter mentions an arrangement to repay June if the house sold. Kit says their parent later changed their mind. There is no signed revision.

choices.label: Seek a careful independent reading of the records

chapters.title: The valuation
chapters.text: The house is worth less than the family imagined. Repair costs matter. A quick sale can fund independence; keeping it can preserve a room someone still needs.

choices.label: Ask for a simple sale estimate

chapters.title: A room with a cost
chapters.text: June would like to stay temporarily. Kit needs cash to move. Ellis cannot meet both needs by pretending the roof fixes itself.

choices.label: Offer a dated stay with shared costs
Sell and discuss a voluntary contribution

chapters.title: What the house cannot decide
chapters.text: An adviser explains the uncertain records; nobody can turn a missing agreement into a certain memory. The family must choose how much certainty to claim.

choices.label: Keep the uncertainty visible in our agreement
Proceed with a sale on the documented position

chapters.title: The kitchen table
chapters.text: Ellis, Kit and June meet beside a list of costs. Whether this becomes a workable arrangement depends on who has actually been heard.

choices.label: Close the house and keep the records

chapters.title: The moving van
chapters.text: The house is being emptied. Ellis finds a child's drawing beneath a drawer: another memory, not another title deed.

choices.label: Share what we can, then let the house go
Leave a complete archive with the family

chapters.title: A home with an agreement
chapters.text: June has a temporary room, Kit has a clear share of costs and future plans, and Ellis has fewer romantic promises. The arrangement is imperfect enough to be real.

chapters.title: The stories we kept
chapters.text: The house is sold or reduced to a manageable arrangement. The family keeps a readable account of the money and the conflicting memories. Losing a building does not require losing every person.

chapters.title: The key in a drawer
chapters.text: The settlement ends the immediate argument. Kit and June take different roads, while Ellis keeps a box of letters that does not explain itself. A closed account is not always a closed story.
